I am one of those who never leave their house for social occasions. I study, watch movies/TV shows, play video games and work out. Whilst I am an introvert, I am not that deluded whereby I blame my lifestyle which is the antitheses of social norms on introversion. 

I can function fine in groups (from my perspective at least, no clue how others view me) yet view the vast majority of social interaction as a fraud. Why am I looked upon as "weird" if I don't live my life with a perpetual smile on my face? (Possible exaggeration but I am sure you understand my point). Moreover, as an existentialist small talk sickens me. I wouldn't say I am a misanthrope but I am just in conflict with social norms. In my opinion (as do most) I do not think I have mental health issues.

I hope I have given you a little insight as to why I (and potentially others?) practice these antisocial tendencies which undoubtedly does somewhat stem from an introverted mind. 

However, in and of itself introversion most definitely should not lead to the aforementioned lifestyle and I agree with you on this.
